result.summary: Re-gate of Step 2b after BACKEND-DEV's rework1 (commit 3191bdc) fixing SECURITY-REVIEWER's Step 2c S10 FAIL. Read `git show 3191bdc` in full (5 files, 141 insertions, 0 deletions -- purely additive). Fix genuinely closes the gap: `getUserForNotificationById` (domain/user.ts) now projects `users.blocked` alongside the existing tgId/lang/chapterDefaultLang fields; `sendPromotionNotification` (handlers/withdraw.ts) adds `if (promotedUser.blocked) { return; }` immediately after the existing null-tgId guard (same silent-skip shape, no effect on the withdrawer's own reply), placed AFTER `getUserForNotificationById`'s read but confirmed it is still BEFORE any of the lang-resolution/message-composition/send code -- the skip is a true short-circuit, not a check that happens too late to matter. Confirmed by reading handlers/withdraw.ts lines 178-227 directly, not from the diff alone. Re-ran the new test myself: `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts -t "S10 rework" --reporter=verbose` -> 1 passed. Confirms: promotion completes (admission=admitted, fresh qrToken, one audit row) for a blocked promoted user, while captured Telegram calls are exactly [answerCallbackQuery, sendMessage] (the sendMessage being the withdrawer's own confirmedReply) -- zero sendMessage to the blocked person's chat_id. Independently constructed a SECOND variant for extra confidence (not copied from BACKEND-DEV's test): a blocked candidate seeded FIRST in waitlist order (earliest created_at) alongside a second, non-blocked waitlisted candidate (later created_at), capacity-1 event, one seat freed. Wrote a throwaway test file apps/bot/src/handlers/_reviewer_scratch_blocked_multi_waitlist.test.ts (own fixtures via createEvent/publishEvent/resolveOrCreateUser, same infra pattern as withdraw.test.ts) and ran it: PASS. Result -- the BLOCKED (earliest) candidate is the one legitimately promoted (admission=admitted, fresh qrToken, one audit row keyed to their registration id) -- confirming blocked status does NOT alter waitlist queue order/eligibility, only the notification is withheld, matching the design's own framing that S10's blocked-skip applies solely to the send step, never to promotion eligibility. The SECOND (non-blocked) candidate is correctly left untouched -- still waitlisted, qrToken still null -- confirming the next-in-line person is not wrongly promoted in the blocked person's place. Zero sendMessage calls reached either candidate's chat_id. Deleted the scratch file immediately after; `git status --porcelain` confirmed clean. No weakening of previously-verified properties: `git diff master...HEAD --stat` (17 files total across the whole run) shows this rework commit itself touches only domain/user.ts (+6/-0), handlers/withdraw.ts (+8/-0), handlers/withdraw.test.ts (+77/-0, new describe block only), docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md (+10/-0), and the rework handoff file -- registration.ts, registration.db.test.ts, and event.ts (the concurrency/lock-order/T-24h/audit-count logic I verified at the original Step 2b PASS) are completely untouched by this commit, confirmed via `git show 3191bdc --stat`. The blocked-skip is a pure early-return inserted after the existing null-tgId guard and before any lang/message-composition/send code -- it cannot affect admission, seat-freeing, or the audit write, all of which committed inside `promoteFromWaitlistIfEligible`'s transaction before `sendPromotionNotification` is ever called (confirmed by reading the call site: handlers/withdraw.ts's confirm handler invokes `withdrawRegistration` -- which commits the promotion -- and only afterward, on `outcome.promotion.kind === 'promoted'`, calls `sendPromotionNotification`). Re-ran the original AC1-AC7 test files together with the new case to confirm no regression: all pass (see commands below). Design doc update (docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md) verified accurate and consistent: §6.1 adds `blocked: boolean` to the `UserForNotification` interface and a comment matching S10's exact wording ("blocked users are skipped in both [transactional and marketing] cases"), matching the actual code. §6.2 adds a clearly-labeled '(SECURITY-REVIEWER Step 2c fix, MINOR)' bullet stating the skip applies to the notification only, not the already-committed promotion -- this matches the actual code and my own independent trace above. Consistent, no drift found. Incidental finding (not blocking this re-gate, filed as an issue below): §6.2's own prose states 'This is the one new "send to someone other than the current ctx's own user" call site in this codebase... no existing handler does this today (checked directly: every ctx.reply(...) call in apps/bot/src/handlers/*.ts replies to the same chat the update came from).' This claim was already present at the original Step 1/2b PASS (unchanged by this commit) and is factually inaccurate: apps/bot/src/handlers/staff.ts (REQ-018, predates REQ-023) already sends `ctx.api.sendMessage(Number(targetUser.tgId), body)` to the assigned staff member's own chat (not the organizer's) at two call sites (lines 98, 168), and neither of those call sites checks `targetUser.blocked` (getUserByTgUsername doesn't even project it) despite S10 applying identically. This is a pre-existing S10 gap in unrelated, already-shipped code (REQ-018), structurally untouched by this diff -- not something this rework introduced or should fix under this run's scope. Filing as its own issue per core-directives' 'No Issue Left Local-Only' rather than fixing here or silently ignoring it. COMMANDS RE-RUN MYSELF, REAL OUTPUT: `npm run lint` (repo root) -> exit 0, 0 errors, 2 pre-existing unrelated apps/web LCP warnings only (unchanged). `npm run build` (repo root) -> exit 0, both workspaces clean. `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://bot:bot@localhost:55432/bot npx vitest run --no-file-parallelism` (repo root, scratch Postgres bot-postgres-1 already running) -> 17 files / 212 tests passed, 0 failed, 0 skipped -- matches BACKEND-DEV's reported count exactly (211->212, the one new S10-rework case), independently re-run by me. `npx vitest run apps/bot/src/handlers/withdraw.test.ts -t "S10 rework" --reporter=verbose` -> 1 passed (the specific new case). My own scratch multi-waitlist variant -> 1 passed, then deleted. Scope check: `git show 3191bdc --stat` touches exactly domain/user.ts, handlers/withdraw.ts, handlers/withdraw.test.ts, docs/agents/design/REQ-023.md, and the rework handoff bookkeeping file -- nothing else. No scope creep. No new npm workspace, no apps/* rename, no build-output move -- no scratch `docker build` required per my role file's trigger condition. `git status --porcelain` clean after deleting my own scratch test file.
